fully before you ask for the next: the command gives no new question until the last answer is written. Answer from her
records (made available to you as described below) and your own medical knowledge; say so when the records do not
settle something.

{"answer": "…", "short": "…",
  "items": [{"n": 1, "says": "…", "why": "…", "confidence": "high",

  "knowledge": {"says": "…", "guideline": "…"},
  "links": [{"from": 0, "to": 1, "says": "…"}]}]}

- "items": each point of your reply that rests on her records or your knowledge (at most 10, most important

  or low), and its chain:

    "field", the one field of it your point rests on: "value" (its own result), "status", "code", "name", "id",
    "date" (when it happened), "start", "end", "recorded" or "text" (words of its text, such as a note or a report's
    conclusion); with "text", "quote", the words your point rests on, copied exactly from that entry's text. When the

    short name, as the read's legend names it ("S3").

    February", "after the stool test", "in the last year"), since only a record from that day on would count against

    guideline you have in mind if you can name one. It is yours, not the records'.
  - "links", when you draw any: that one of your facts bears on another, as {"from": <fact's place, from 0>, "to":

[{"from": {"item": <n>, "fact": <place>}, "to": {"item": <n>, "fact": <place>}, "says": "how"}].

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

checkup.answer:
Here is what I would raise at your check-up, based on the records I can see.

1. Your stool test (FIT) from 4 November 2025 was positive. The records show no colonoscopy or other follow-up test after it. A positive FIT normally needs a colonoscopy to look for the cause, so please ask your doctor whether that has happened or is still needed. This is the most important item.

2. Your diabetes blood test (HbA1c) was last recorded on 16 February 2026, about eight and a half months ago. It was 6.9%, down from 8.3% in January 2025, so your numbers have improved. Diabetes usually needs this test every three to six months, so it is probably due now.

3. Your LDL ("bad") cholesterol was 131 mg/dL in February 2025, above the target of 99 or lower, and you started atorvastatin around then. The records show no cholesterol panel since then. A recheck is usually done a few weeks to a few months after starting a statin and then regularly. It may have been done somewhere the records do not show, so check with your doctor.

4. The records show no urine albumin test (a urine test for kidney protein leakage, sometimes called UACR). Your kidney filtration (eGFR) was 69 in February 2026, which is in the normal range. With diabetes, a yearly urine albumin test is usually recommended, so ask whether you have had one.

5. The records contain no vaccinations at all. This may only mean they are not in this record. At your age and with diabetes, your doctor can check which vaccines you are due.

6. The records show Jardiance started around February 2025 but have no start date for it, and metformin ended in April 2024. It would help to confirm with your doctor when you began Jardiance, so your medication history is complete.

One reassuring result: a chest CT in July 2025 showed no pulmonary embolism (a blood clot in the lung), and that suspicion was ruled out.
checkup.short: Positive FIT stool test from Nov 2025 with no follow-up colonoscopy recorded; HbA1c last checked Feb 2026 and likely due; no cholesterol recheck since starting atorvastatin in Feb 2025 (LDL 131); no urine albumin test recorded; no vaccinations recorded; Jardiance start date missing.

checkup.answer:
Here is what your records suggest bringing up at your check-up, most important first.

1. A positive stool test (FIT) from 4 November 2025. Your records show a positive result and no colonoscopy or other follow-up test since. A positive FIT normally needs a colonoscopy to look for the cause, such as polyps or cancer. Please ask whether this was followed up. If it was not, this is the most urgent item.

2. Your HbA1c (blood sugar average) is due. The last one was 6.9% on 16 February 2026, down from 8.3% in January 2025. Nothing has been recorded since, which is over eight months ago.

3. Your LDL ("bad") cholesterol was 131 mg/dL on 18 February 2025, which is high. Atorvastatin was prescribed two days later, and there is no cholesterol test since. Ask for a lipid panel to see how the statin is working.

4. Your kidney function (eGFR) fell from 73 to 69 over the year. It is still in the normal range, but the trend is worth checking. No urine albumin test is recorded. People with diabetes usually have this checked yearly, so ask about it.

5. Metformin was stopped in April 2024, and the records do not say why. Your HbA1c rose after that. Ask your doctor for the reason and whether your current diabetes plan still fits.

6. No diabetic eye exam or foot exam is recorded. Ask about both. They may have happened somewhere that is not in these records.

7. No vaccines are recorded at all. Ask about flu, pneumonia, shingles and tetanus boosters. Vaccines given at a pharmacy may not appear here.

8. Nothing to act on here: the chest CT angiogram in July 2025 showed no pulmonary embolism, and the chest wall pain has resolved. The raised D-dimer blood test from that time is explained by the normal CT result.

checkup.answer:
Here is what I would raise at your check-up, most important first. The records I have run to 15 October 2026, so anything done at another clinic or after that date will not show here. Please check these points with your doctor.

1. Your stool test (FIT) from 4 November 2025 came back positive. I cannot find a colonoscopy or any other bowel follow-up after it. A positive result normally leads to a colonoscopy, so this is the most urgent item. If that has not happened, call the office before your appointment.

2. Metformin was stopped on 15 April 2024, and the records give no reason. Your next diabetes medicine, empagliflozin (Jardiance), was not started until 20 February 2025. Over that gap your A1c (a blood sugar average over about three months) rose from 6.7% to 8.3%. Ask why metformin was stopped and whether you went without diabetes treatment.

3. Your last A1c was 6.9% on 16 February 2026. That is more than eight months ago. With diabetes it is usually checked at least every six months, so it is due.

4. Cholesterol: in February 2025 your LDL was 131 and your total cholesterol was 212, both high. You started atorvastatin on 20 February 2025. No cholesterol test has been recorded since, so a recheck is probably due.

5. Kidneys: your eGFR (a kidney filtering number) was 69 in February 2026, down from 73 a year earlier. That is still above the usual cut-off of 60. No urine albumin test appears anywhere in the records. People with diabetes normally have one every year.

6. Blood count: none appears in the records. Since your stool test was positive, ask whether a blood count should be checked for anemia, which can come from slow bleeding.

7. Blood pressure: no reading appears anywhere in these records. Ask for one at the check-up.

8. Your condition list still includes pulmonary embolism (a clot in the lung). The CT scan in July 2025 found no clot, and the entry is marked as refuted. Ask your doctor to confirm it is not a current diagnosis and to correct the list.

9. Diabetes checks: I see no eye exam (retinal or dilated) and no foot exam recorded. Both are usually done every year for diabetes.

The records may be incomplete, for example if other clinics ran tests, so treat this as a list of questions for your doctor rather than a diagnosis.

1. Your stool test (FIT) on 4 Nov 2025 was positive, and I see nothing after it. A positive FIT normally needs a colonoscopy, ideally within a few months. 2. Your diabetes check is due. Your last A1c was 6.9% on 16 Feb 2026, more than 8 months ago. Diabetes is usually rechecked every 3 to 6 months. The trend is good: your A1c rose to 8.3% in Jan 2025 after metformin ended in April 2024, then fell to 7.6%, 7.1% and 6.9% after Jardiance (empagliflozin) was started in Feb 2025. The records do not say why metformin was stopped, so ask whether that was a deliberate decision and whether Jardiance alone is still the plan.

checkup.answer:
Here is what I would bring up at your check-up, most important first. This comes from your records and general medical guidance. I can only see what is in these records, so check with your doctor about anything that happened elsewhere.

1. Lung nodule scan. A CT on October 18, 2025 found a 7 mm spot in your right lower lung. The radiologist advised a non-contrast chest CT in 6-12 months, a window that closed in October 2026. I see no such scan, and it is not mentioned at your June 2026 visit.

2. Thyroid recheck. Your TSH was high (7.9) on March 3, 2026. The hospital asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated 6-8 weeks after discharge. I see no repeat test.

3. Hydrochlorothiazide (a water pill). The hospital stopped it on March 5, 2026 because your sodium had dropped to 123. But your pharmacy record still shows it as active with refills left, and a May 2026 eye clinic medication list shows it as active too. Please confirm whether you are still taking it. Your sodium was 134 on June 15, 2026, and I see no recheck since. The low sodium is also not on your allergy list, so ask for it to be recorded.

4. Cholesterol and statin. Your LDL cholesterol was 142 in September 2025, and I see no repeat test. You have type 2 diabetes, and I see no statin on your medication list. Ask whether you should be on one.

5. Kidney urine test. Diabetes usually calls for a yearly urine test for early kidney damage (albumin-to-creatinine ratio). I see none. Your kidney filtration was normal in June (eGFR 71).

6. Flu shot. Your last flu shot was November 8, 2025. None is recorded for this season.

7. Shingles vaccine. You had one Shingrix dose on November 8, 2025. The second dose is normally due 2-6 months later, and I see none.

8. Kidney stone follow-up. The October 2025 stone was 4 mm, and your urine showed large amounts of blood. The discharge plan said to see urology if it had not passed within 2 weeks. I see no later urine test or urology visit confirming it passed.

9. Medication list. Amlodipine, losartan and metformin each appear more than once from different sources, and some entries are patient-reported. Bring your bottles to the visit so the list can be cleaned up.

Things that look on track: blood pressure 128/80 in June (at goal), A1c 6.6% in June, an eye exam on May 14, 2026 with no diabetic eye damage (next due about May 2027), and a normal colonoscopy in 2019 (next due about 2029). Your next primary care visit is due around December 2026.

checkup.answer:
Here is what I found, most urgent first. Your most recent record is dated July 14, 2026, so anything after that is not in what I have.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide (a water pill). Kestrel Harbor Hospital stopped it on March 5, 2026. Your sodium had fallen to 123, and you were admitted with dizziness after a fall at home. The discharge instructions say to stop it. But the pharmacy refilled it on April 2, 2026 with two refills left, and it still shows as active. On May 14 you told the eye clinic you were taking it, and your sodium on June 15 was still a little low (134). Your clinic's June 15 note says to continue current medications. Please call Dr. Marsh and the pharmacy this week to confirm whether you should be taking it. If it is stopped, ask for the refills to be cancelled, and ask whether your blood pressure plan needs changing. Seek urgent care for confusion, severe headache, vomiting, or fainting.

2. Lung nodule. A CT on October 18, 2025 (done for the kidney stone) found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the right lower lung. The radiologist recommended a non-contrast chest CT in 6 to 12 months. That window ended October 18, 2026, and your records contain no chest CT. Being a never-smoker lowers the risk, but the recommendation still needs to be scheduled or deliberately declined.

3. Kidney stone follow-up. A 4 mm stone sits at the right ureter junction, and the urine test showed large blood. The instructions said to see your primary doctor within a week, and to see urology if the stone had not passed in two weeks. Your records show no urology visit, no repeat urine test, and no note confirming the stone passed.

4. Thyroid recheck. TSH was 7.9 (high) on March 3, 2026, with a normal free T4 (1.0). The hospital asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated 6 to 8 weeks after discharge, which is about late April. No repeat is recorded.

5. Cholesterol and a statin. On September 22, 2025 your LDL was 142 (high), HDL 48 (low), and triglycerides 155 (high). You have had type 2 diabetes since September 2025. No statin appears on any medication list, and there is no cholesterol test after September 2025. Guidelines usually recommend a statin for adults with diabetes in your age range, so ask whether one was discussed.

6. Vaccines. The pharmacy gave you a flu shot, the first Shingrix (shingles) dose, and Prevnar 20 on November 8, 2025. The second Shingrix dose was due 2 to 6 months later and is not recorded. Your clinic's copy lists only the October 2024 flu shot, so it may not have the November vaccines. There is no 2026-27 flu shot and no COVID-19 vaccine in any record.

7. Lists that do not match. Lisinopril was stopped in September 2025 for a dry cough. Only your clinic's copy records it as an intolerance. The hospital, eye clinic and pharmacy allergy lists show only aspirin. The aspirin reaction (hives) was recorded as mild in April 2025 and as moderate from May 2025 on. Ask them to correct both.

8. Refills. Losartan, metformin and amlodipine were last filled June 28, 2026 for 90 days, so the supply runs out around late September. I cannot see anything after July 14, so check that you have refills.

9. Diabetes. Your A1c has come down from 6.9% to 6.7% to 6.6% (June 15, 2026). Your eye exam on May 14, 2026 showed no diabetic retinopathy. Two gaps: no urine albumin test is recorded since diagnosis, and the yearly kidney urine check is missing. Your kidney function (eGFR 71) is normal. The next A1c is due around December 2026.

10. Screenings not in these records. No mammogram or cervical screening appears. Your colonoscopy in April 2019 was normal, so the next one is due around 2029.

What looks fine: your potassium has been normal throughout, and your June 2026 blood pressure of 128/80 was at goal. This is a summary of your records and general guidelines, not a diagnosis. Your doctors can confirm each item.

Here's what I'd bring to your check-up, most urgent first. It's based on your records and general medical guidelines; Dr. Marsh makes the final calls.

1. **Hydrochlorothiazide (water pill): check this first.** The hospital stopped it on March 5, 2026 because your sodium was low (123). But your clinic list still shows it as active in June, the pharmacy refilled it on April 2 with two refills left, and on May 14 you listed it as a medicine you take. Your June 15 sodium was 134, still low, and the clinic note from that day says 'continue current medications' without mentioning sodium. If you're still taking it, call Dr. Marsh's office today to confirm, and ask the pharmacy to cancel the refills. Ask for a sodium recheck. In March you were also dizzy and had a fall at home, so mention any dizziness when you stand up. Get urgent care for confusion, a bad headache, vomiting or unsteadiness.

2. **Lung nodule: follow-up scan overdue.** A CT on October 18, 2025 showed a 7 mm solid spot in your right lower lung. The radiologist advised a repeat chest CT in 6 to 12 months, so by October 18, 2026. There is no repeat scan in your records, and no later note mentions the spot.

3. **Thyroid test not repeated.** Your TSH was high on March 3, 2026 (7.9), with a normal free T4. The hospital asked for a repeat in 6 to 8 weeks, meaning mid to late April. None is on record, including the June labs.

4. **Cholesterol and statin.** On September 22, 2025 your total cholesterol was 221, LDL 142, HDL 48 (low) and triglycerides 155. With diabetes and high blood pressure, guidelines usually recommend a statin at your age. No statin is on any list, no note explains why not, and your yearly cholesterol check is due. Ask Dr. Marsh whether a statin is right for you.

5. **Kidney stone follow-up.** An October 2025 ER CT showed a 4 mm stone where the right ureter enters the bladder, with mild kidney swelling, and urine testing showed large blood (3+). The ER asked for a primary-care visit within a week, and urology if the stone hadn't passed in two weeks. Your records don't show either visit, a repeat urine test, or that the stone passed. The stone is also missing from your clinic problem lists. Ask whether the blood in your urine has cleared.

6. **Second Shingrix shot missing.** You had dose one on November 8, 2025. Dose two is due 2 to 6 months later, and no record shows it. It can still be given now without starting over.

7. **Lisinopril cough missing from most allergy lists.** Your clinic lists lisinopril as an intolerance (dry cough, 2025). The hospital, eye clinic and pharmacy lists show only aspirin. Ask for the lisinopril cough to be added to every list.

checkup.answer:
Priya, going through your records, these are the things I would bring up, most important first.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide (HCTZ). In March 2026 you were in Kestrel Harbor Hospital for three days with a sodium of 123, dizziness and a fall. The hospital blamed the HCTZ and told you to stop it. But the pharmacy refilled it on April 2, 2026 (90 days, 2 refills left) and still lists it as active. You told the eye clinic in May that you take it, and Dr. Marsh's June 2026 list still shows it as a current daily medicine. The records can't tell me whether you are actually still taking it. Please check your pill bottles, and ask Dr. Marsh and the pharmacy to cancel it if it was meant to be stopped.

2. Your sodium was still a little low in June 2026 (134, normal is 135 to 145), about three months after the hospital stay. I can't say why. Continuing the HCTZ is one possibility, but nothing in the records settles it. A repeat blood test is reasonable.

3. A lung nodule that needs a repeat scan. The CT you had in the ER for the kidney stone on October 18, 2025 found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the lower right lung. The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months. That window ran from April to October 18, 2026, and I see no chest CT in your records. The nodule isn't on any problem list, and the ER discharge instructions never mention it. You've never smoked, which is reassuring, but this follow-up scan is now due or overdue. Please raise it first.

4. Thyroid retest. In the hospital your TSH was high (7.9) with a normal free T4. The discharge note asked for both to be repeated in 6 to 8 weeks. I find no repeat in your records. A TSH can be temporarily high during an illness, so a repeat is how you find out if it matters.

5. Your regular clinic's chart looks incomplete. Fernhill Family Clinic's records through June 2026 don't mention the March hospital stay, the low sodium, the kidney stone, or the lung nodule. I see no visit after the hospital stay (you were told to follow up in 1 to 2 weeks) or after the ER visit (1 week). Nothing shows the kidney stone passing or a urology visit. Bring the hospital and ER papers so Dr. Marsh has the full picture.

6. Diabetes care gaps. Your A1c has improved (6.9, then 6.7, then 6.6% in June 2026) and your June 2026 dilated eye exam showed no diabetic eye damage, which is good. But your LDL cholesterol was 142 in September 2025 (total 221, HDL 48, triglycerides 155) and I see no cholesterol medicine and no repeat lipid test. I also see no urine albumin test, no foot exam, and no record that the diabetes education referral from September 2025 happened. Ask whether a statin is right for you, and about these checks. Your next A1c is around December 2026, six months after the June visit.

7. Vaccines. On November 8, 2025 the pharmacy gave you flu, Shingrix dose 1, and Prevnar 20 (pneumococcal, which is complete). Shingrix needs a second dose 2 to 6 months after the first, so it was due between January and May 2026. I find no second dose. I also see no flu shot for this fall, though my records end in July 2026. Fernhill's vaccine list still shows only the October 2024 flu shot, so tell them about the pharmacy shots.

8. Allergy lists don't match. The cough you had on lisinopril (September 2025) is only on Fernhill's list, not on the hospital's, the pharmacy's, or the eye clinic's. If HCTZ did cause the low sodium, it should be recorded as an adverse reaction too. The hospital's early records call your aspirin reaction mild, but its later records call it moderate. Ask to have these made consistent.

9. Screening. Your colonoscopy in April 2019 was normal, with a repeat advised in 10 years, so it is not due until about 2029. I see no mammogram or cervical screening results in these records. They may simply be held elsewhere, so check when you last had them.

This is not medical advice to change any medicine on your own. Confirm what you are taking with your doctor or pharmacist.

checkup.answer:
Your records run only to mid-July 2026, so anything since then is not visible to me. Here is what I would bring up, most important first.

1. Hydrochlorothiazide may still be in your routine. In March 2026 you were in the hospital for 3 days with a sodium of 123, and the discharge papers say to STOP hydrochlorothiazide because it was the likely cause. The hospital record shows it discontinued on March 5. But the pharmacy refilled it on April 2 for 90 days and still shows it active with 2 refills left. Your family clinic's June 2026 summary also still lists it as a current medicine, and does not mention the hyponatremia. Your sodium on June 15 was low again at 134. Please check whether you are taking it. If you are, tell Dr. Marsh and the pharmacy right away. If you are not, ask for the pharmacy and clinic lists to be corrected. The reaction should also be added to your allergy and intolerance list, as lisinopril's cough already is.

2. The lung nodule has not been followed up. The CT done in the ER on October 18, 2025 (for the kidney stone) found an incidental 7 mm solid nodule in the right lower lung. The radiologist recommended a chest CT in 6 to 12 months. That window ended around October 18, 2026, and I find no chest CT and no mention of the nodule in your clinic notes or problem list. You have never smoked, which lowers the risk, but this follow-up is due now.

3. The thyroid recheck is missing. Your TSH was high (7.9) on March 3, 2026 with a normal free T4 (1.0). The hospital asked for both to be repeated in 6 to 8 weeks. I see no repeat. Low sodium can also be linked to an underactive thyroid, so this matters for item 1 too.

4. Vaccines. Shingrix needs a second dose 2 to 6 months after the first. You had dose 1 at the pharmacy on November 8, 2025, and I find no dose 2. Your last flu shot on record was that same day, so the 2026-27 shot is not recorded yet. I also find no hepatitis B vaccine, which is generally advised for adults with diabetes under 60, and no Tdap or COVID shots. Those may simply be recorded elsewhere. Your pneumococcal (Prevnar 20) shot is done.

5. Cholesterol and statin. In September 2025 your LDL was 142, HDL 48 and triglycerides 155. No statin appears on any medication list and no repeat lipid panel appears. Adults aged 40 to 75 with diabetes are generally offered a statin, so ask whether you should start one.

6. Diabetes checks. Your A1c has come down well, 6.9 to 6.7 to 6.6 in June 2026, and your dilated eye exam in May 2026 showed no retinopathy (next due May 2027). I find no urine albumin-to-creatinine test, no documented foot exam, and no record that the diabetes education referral from September 2025 happened. Ask about all three. Your next A1c is due around December 2026, when Dr. Marsh asked to see you.

7. Kidney stone follow-up. The ER asked for a primary-care visit within a week and urology if the stone had not passed in 2 weeks. I find no record of either, nor any note on whether the stone passed. It is also absent from your clinic problem list.

8. Details that do not match across records. The aspirin reaction is described as mild in two early 2025 hospital summaries and as moderate in later ones. The lisinopril cough appears in the clinic's allergy list but not the hospital's. Worth asking everyone to align them. Because aspirin gives you hives, you were also kept off ibuprofen and ketorolac in the ER, so ask your doctor about NSAID safety.

9. Screening. Your colonoscopy on April 16, 2019 was normal with a 10-year repeat, so it is not due until about 2029. I find no mammogram or cervical screening in any of these records, so ask when they were last done.

checkup.answer:
Your records come from six places (Kestrel Harbor Hospital, Fernhill Family Clinic, Saltmarsh ED, Northbay Labs, Clearwater Eye and Alder Street Pharmacy), and they stop in mid-July 2026. Anything done since then, or done somewhere that isn't in them, won't show up here. Here is what I would raise, most important first.

1. A lung nodule that was never followed up (most urgent). The CT you had in the Saltmarsh ER on Oct 18, 2025 for the kidney stone also picked up a 7 mm solid nodule in the lower right lung. The radiologist recommended a non-contrast chest CT in 6-12 months, so the window ran from April to Oct 18, 2026 and has now closed. I find no chest CT and no mention of the nodule anywhere else. Most nodules like this are harmless, and you have never smoked, which lowers the risk. It still needs that scan, so ask for it now.

2. Hydrochlorothiazide: the records disagree about whether you should be taking it. You were admitted to Kestrel Harbor on March 2, 2026 with dizziness, a fall and a sodium of 123. The hospital blamed hydrochlorothiazide and told you to stop it on March 5. But Alder Street Pharmacy filled it on April 2 (90 days, 2 refills left, still marked active), you told the eye clinic on May 14 that you take it, and Fernhill's June 2026 list still shows it as active. Your sodium was low again (134) on June 15. The pharmacy did not refill it on June 28 the way it did your other pills, so you may have stopped. The records can't tell me. Please tell Dr. Marsh exactly what you are taking, and don't start or stop anything on the strength of this note alone.

3. A thyroid recheck that was asked for and not done. Your TSH was mildly high (7.9) during the March stay, with a normal free T4. The discharge instructions asked for TSH and free T4 to be repeated in 6-8 weeks, which would have been around late April. I see no repeat.

4. Fernhill doesn't seem to know about your outside care. Dr. Marsh's problem list (June 2026) shows hay fever, high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes. It doesn't show the kidney stone, the lung nodule or the March hospital stay. The ER asked you to see your primary care doctor within a week, and the hospital asked for a visit within 1-2 weeks. I find no visit or note about either. Nothing records whether the stone passed or whether you saw urology. It's worth bringing the discharge papers.

5. Cholesterol. Your LDL was 142 and HDL 48 in Sept 2025, and it has not been rechecked. You have diabetes, and you are 57. Guidelines generally advise a statin for people aged 40-75 with diabetes. No statin appears on any of your medication lists and no discussion of one is recorded. Ask whether one is right for you.

6. Diabetes checks that aren't in the records. Your A1c is improving (6.9, then 6.7, then 6.6) and your June 2026 kidney function was normal. But I find no urine albumin-to-creatinine test, which is recommended yearly for people with diabetes, and no foot exam. You were referred to diabetes education in Sept 2025, but nothing shows you went. (The ER urine dipstick showed no protein, but that isn't the same test.)

7. Vaccines. On Nov 8, 2025 the pharmacy gave you flu, Prevnar 20 and the first Shingrix. The second Shingrix dose is normally due 2-6 months after the first, and none is recorded. No flu shot is recorded since November 2025, so this season's dose may be due. I also find no record of tetanus (Td/Tdap), COVID or hepatitis B vaccines, which are commonly advised for adults with diabetes. These may simply have been given somewhere else.

8. Women's cancer screening. I see no mammogram and no cervical screening (Pap or HPV test) anywhere. These are often done at outside centers, so they may exist. If you can't find them, ask about getting them, since you turn 58 on Nov 4.

9. Allergy lists don't match. Fernhill lists lisinopril (dry cough) as an intolerance, but the hospital, ER, pharmacy and eye clinic lists show only aspirin. The hospital's own medication list says lisinopril was stopped for cough. Also, your aspirin reaction was recorded as mild in April 2025 and as moderate from May 2025 on. Ask each place to update its list.

10. Things that look on track. Your colonoscopy on April 16, 2019 was normal, with a repeat advised in 10 years (2029). Your dilated eye exam on May 14, 2026 showed no diabetic retinopathy, and the eye clinic wants you back in 12 months. Your blood pressure on June 15, 2026 was 128/80, which Dr. Marsh called at goal.

This is a review of your paperwork, not a diagnosis. Dr. Marsh can sort out what applies to you.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

Discharge instructions, March 5, 2026.
You were admitted with dizziness and a low sodium level (123). Your sodium improved after hydrochlorothiazide was stopped and with fluid restriction.
STOP taking hydrochlorothiazide. Continue losartan 50 mg once daily, amlodipine 5 mg once daily and metformin ER 500 mg with the evening meal.
Follow up with your primary care provider, Elena Marsh, MD, at Fernhill Family Clinic within 1-2 weeks.
Your thyroid test (TSH) was mildly high during your stay. Please have TSH and free T4 repeated in 6-8 weeks, once you have recovered.

STOP taking hydrochlorothiazide. Continue losartan 50 mg once daily, amlodipine 5 mg once daily and metformin ER 500 mg with the evening meal.
Follow up with your primary care provider, Elena Marsh, MD, at Fernhill Family Clinic within 1-2 weeks.
Your thyroid test (TSH) was mildly high during your stay. Please have TSH and free T4 repeated in 6-8 weeks, once you have recovered.

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.

<paragraph>September 22, 2025 (annual visit, Elena Marsh, MD): Fasting glucose 138 and hemoglobin A1c 6.9%: new diagnosis of type 2 diabetes. Start metformin ER 500 mg with the evening meal; referred to diabetes education. Dry cough for several months on lisinopril: stop lisinopril, start losartan 50 mg daily. Continue amlodipine 5 mg.</paragraph>
Discontinued September 22, 2025 by outside provider (cough); replaced by losartan
<paragraph>STOP taking hydrochlorothiazide. Continue losartan 50 mg once daily, amlodipine 5 mg once daily and metformin ER 500 mg with the evening meal.</paragraph>

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

fields: Note or document entry · Plan of care note · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

Discharge instructions, October 18, 2025.
You were seen for a kidney stone on the right side. The stone is small (4 mm) and is likely to pass on its own.
Take tamsulosin 0.4 mg once a day for 14 days to help the stone pass. Use acetaminophen for pain and ondansetron if you feel sick to your stomach. Ibuprofen and ketorolac were not given because of your aspirin allergy.
Drink plenty of fluids and strain your urine. Follow up with your primary care provider in 1 week. If the stone has not passed in 2 weeks, see urology.
Return to the emergency department for fever, pain that is not controlled, or vomiting that does not stop.

fields: Note or document entry · Relevant diagnostic tests/laboratory data Narrative · 2025-10-18T12:55:12Z

CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITHOUT CONTRAST (performed October 18, 2025 07:52 UTC; accession SRM-CT-2510-88412)
Indication: Right flank pain radiating to the groin, hematuria.
Technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis without intravenous or oral contrast. Dose reduction technique was used.
Findings: There is a 4 mm calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis and mild perinephric stranding. No other renal or ureteral calculi. The left kidney is unremarkable. The liver, gallbladder, spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands are unremarkable for a non-contrast study. The appendix is normal. No bowel obstruction. No free fluid. The urinary bladder is decompressed. Uterus and adnexa are unremarkable. Lung bases: a 7 mm solid nodule is present in the right lower lobe (series 2, image 14). No pleural effusion. No acute osseous abnormality.
Impression: 1. 4 mm obstructing calculus at the right ureterovesical junction with mild right hydroureteronephrosis. 2. Incidental 7 mm solid pulmonary nodule in the right lower lobe, partially imaged. Per Fleischner Society guidelines, a non-contrast CT of the chest is recommended in 6-12 months.
Electronically signed by Hannah Lindqvist, MD (Radiology), October 18, 2025 08:31 UTC.

items.reason: Item 5 names the missing urine albumin (uACR) test, with yearly diabetes screening as the reason, and sets it against eGFR 69 and 73. The diabetes condition itself is not cited as a fact in that item.
Names the positive FIT of 4 Nov 2025 and says no colonoscopy or booking is in the records; says a diagnostic colonoscopy is needed. Does not offer a repeat stool test.

States she is on empagliflozin and that her last A1c was 6.9 (Feb 2026). The 8.3 peak is framed as past and 'come down since'. No untreated claim, no 'A1c 8.3 now', no restart-metformin advice. The ask-whether-you-take-it line is neutral.

Says the PE entry is marked ruled out and the CT showed no PE. Only a soft 'you may want to ask about the high D-dimer'; it does not say the D-dimer was not followed up. Borderline nudge, not the trap.

beyond.why: A1c not repeated for 8.5 months: PT6, a legitimate find.
LDL 131 two days before atorvastatin with no repeat lipid panel: PT7, a legitimate find.
No diabetic eye exam in the records: a valid absence listed in PT5, neutral.

skipped: the type 2 diabetes condition fact; the diabetes link rests on the knowledge line only

items.reason: Names the missing urine albumin / UACR test and says a yearly test is recommended with diabetes. The diabetes link cites a fact 2 that is not in the item.
Names the positive FIT of 4 Nov 2025 with no colonoscopy after it, and asks whether one has happened or is still needed. Does not offer a repeat stool test and does not say nothing further is needed.
Gives the A1c as 6.9 on 16 Feb 2026, down from 8.3 in Jan 2025 ('your numbers have improved'). Does not say untreated, does not give 8.3 as current, does not suggest restarting metformin.
Says the July 2025 CT showed no PE and that the suspicion was ruled out. Not raised as a clot.

beyond.why: HbA1c not repeated since Feb 2026: PT6, a legitimate find.
LDL 131 with no lipid panel since atorvastatin: PT7, a legitimate find. The LDL target of 99 or lower is a general threshold, not from the records, but is reasonable.
No vaccinations at all in the records: a valid absence listed in PT5, neutral; the answer hedges that the records may simply not hold them.
The Jardiance entry has a recorded date (20 Feb 2025) and no start date; a fair observation about the record's form, not planted.

skipped: the 2025 eGFR of 73 needed for the yearly eGFR link
